title: Stability lanes: cohort orchestration, cross-surface compatibility and upgrade shield
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a coherent 'stability lanes' model (LTS / Stable / Fast) that maps across runtime, public API, SDKs, and Console. Deliver a support matrix, rollout gates, and an automated "upgrade shield" (preflight validators + telemetry gates) so teams can safely adopt new versions with predictable rollback semantics. Scope covers: taxonomy of lanes and expected compatibility guarantees; semantic versioning policy and pinning rules across surfaces; automated compatibility test suite (contract + fuzz + perf); cohort orchestration model for canarying; rollout gating signals and thresholds; and a minimal set of operator tools (upgrade-check CLI, rollout advisor, and compatibility dashboard). This ticket is the engineering implementation plan and orchestration prototype for the stability lanes initiative.
acceptance_criteria: Documented support matrix that lists compatibility guarantees for runtime, public API, SDKs (python/js), and Console for each stability lane
A minimal rollout choreography prototype that executes a canary cohort (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automated gates and rollback hooks
An 'upgrade-check' tool that runs the compatibility-suite and emits a pass/fail with human-readable remediation steps
Telemetry gating implemented in the prototype: latency P95 < 1.5x baseline, error rate increase < 0.5pp, and token throughput within 10% of baseline
Runbook and postmortem template for failed rollouts included in the repo and Console links
decisions: Adopt 'stability lanes' naming: LTS (18 month support), Stable (6 month), Fast (continuous). Guarantees vary by lane: strong API+wire contract for LTS, behavioral stability and opt-in features for Stable, experimental toggles for Fast.
Use semantic versioning with a compatibility-claim header in the packaged manifest for each surface (runtime, api, sdk, console) so automated validators can reason about expected breaking changes.
Rollouts will use cohort percentages and automated rollback based on telemetry gates; manual abort remains possible for high-severity anomalies.
The Console will show model/surface pins and an 'upgrade advisor' that suggests routes based on customer SLA and pinned versions.
tradeoffs: Stronger LTS guarantees increase maintenance cost and slow feature velocity for LTS branches.
Strict automated gates reduce erroneous rollouts but will require investment in reliability of tests and synthetic workload generation.
Surface-by-surface pinning (runtime vs SDK) yields operational clarity at the cost of more complex rollout choreography.
Providing a single monolithic compatibility-suite is easier to operate but risks becoming slow; we choose modular suites for contract/fuzz/perf to allow parallelization.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design + spec (this ticket). Phase 1: Proof-of-concept cohort orchestration for runtime only (small customer subset). Phase 2: Expand compatibility-suite to API and SDKs and run in staging. Phase 3: Integrate Console advisor and pinning UI; pilot LTS lane for a single minor runtime upgrade. Canary progression: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with minimum 24-hour observation windows and mandatory health checks between steps. Emergency rollback triggers: service-error-rate delta > 0.5pp or latency P95 > 1.5x baseline sustained for 30 minutes.
tooling_requirements: upgrade-check CLI: runs contract tests, schema diff, and basic perf microbenchmarks
compatibility-suite: modular test harness for contract, fuzz, and perf tests; produces machine-readable verdicts
cohort-orchestrator: simple controller that can move traffic percentages with roll-forward / rollback primitives
console-integrations: UI for pins, advisor, and visualized rollouts (with link to runbooks)
automated preflight that runs on PRs touching public interfaces and announces compatibility risk
telemetry_and_gates: Primary signals: request error rate, latency P95, request throughput, model-token throughput, memory OOM alerts
Health gates: error-rate increase < 0.5 percentage points; latency P95 < 1.5x baseline; no OOMs or instance-level fatal alerts
Regression detection: change point detection within the first 6 hours; rolling 1h and 24h windows for early and medium-term regressions
Quality gates tie into Console alerts and will automatically pause further cohort progression if breached
